## NEW THIS SCAN (2026-08-14) — five additions

### Enable incoming A2A on a Foundry agent (preview)  ** freshest item in this scan **
/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/enable-agent-to-agent-endpoint — ms.date 2026-08-12, updated 2026-08-13
Exposes a Foundry agent AS an A2A server so other agents can DISCOVER and CALL it. Previously this
monitor had only covered the outgoing direction (agent calls a remote A2A endpoint).
  - Supported: **prompt agents** (all, by default) and hosted agents that implement the responses
    protocol. Incoming A2A REQUIRES the responses protocol.
  - Enabled by one PATCH setting `agent_card` + `agent_endpoint.protocol_configuration.a2a`.
    Not configurable in the Foundry portal yet — REST API or Python SDK (azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0).
  - Protocol versions **1.0 and 0.3** both served on the same base path
    `…/agents/{agent}/endpoint/protocols/a2a`. Version selected via agent-card discovery, the
    `A2A-Version` header, or `?a2a-version=`. **If unspecified, Foundry serves v0.3 by default.**
  - Agent cards published at `…/protocols/a2a/agentCard/v1.0` and `…/agentCard/v0.3`. One authored
    card is projected into both shapes. Card carries description, version, and **skills[]**
    (id / name / description).
  - **All A2A URLs require Microsoft Entra ID auth; anonymous access to the agent card is NOT
    supported.** Caller needs the **Foundry Agent Consumer** role (or higher) on the hosting project.
    Key-based and unauthenticated access unsupported.
  - Two caller auth patterns: **on-behalf-of the end user** (agent sees the real user) and
    **service identity** (agent identity / SP / managed identity — no user context).
  - Agent-to-agent connections use `authType: AgenticIdentityToken`, `category: RemoteA2A`,
    audience https://ai.azure.com. Calling agents use `A2APreviewTool`.
  - Transports: v0.3 = HTTP+JSON and JSONRPC; **v1.0 = JSONRPC only**; gRPC unsupported.
  - Limitations: text modality only; no streaming/SSE; preview.

### Managed MCP servers powered by connector namespaces (preview)
/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/tools/connectors — ms.date 2026-07-28, updated 2026-07-31
  - The Foundry Tools Catalog carries **over 1,000 connectors**. Adding one makes Foundry create a
    **managed MCP server** that Foundry provisions and hosts.
  - Every Foundry account has a **Connector Namespace** — a managed service hosting connector
    runtimes and MCP servers. **Each project maps to an environment in that namespace.** The
    namespace handles hosting, tool definitions, authentication, credential management and lifecycle.
  - Flow: Browse -> Connect (authenticate) -> Select actions -> Add tool. Only the selected connector
    ACTIONS become MCP tools. Triggers are NOT supported.
  - Auth: **OAuth2** in the supported flow. **Each end user that calls the agent must complete a
    one-time OAuth consent** minted per-user via `listConsentLinks` (link valid ~1 hour); service
    principals supply their own objectId/tenantId.
  - Project connection shape: `authType: OAuth2`, `category: RemoteTool`,
    `metadata.type = gateway_connector`, `metadata.toolEntityId`, and
    `metadata.mcpserverConfigProperties` (the operations list + per-operation parameter schema).
    `target` starts as the literal `https://placeholder` and is rewritten by the platform to the real
    gateway URL, of the form
    `https://app-XX.<region>.logic.azure.com/api/connectorGateways/<envId>/mcpServerConfigs/<connectionName>/mcp`
    — i.e. **the managed MCP endpoint is hosted on logic.azure.com, not on the Foundry endpoint.**
    `overallStatus` goes Unauthenticated -> Connected once consent + action registration complete.
  - Publisher tiers with explicitly different data responsibility: **Microsoft internal** (SharePoint,
    Teams, Dynamics 365 — data stays on Microsoft infra), **Microsoft external** (GitHub — transits
    Microsoft infra to the external service), **Verified third-party** (Docusign, Databricks, Box),
    and **Independent publisher** (community-contributed, "lower certification bar").
  - Microsoft's own warning on the page: third-party tools are Non-Microsoft Products, "you do so at
    your own risk", auth keys and prompt content might be passed to the third-party tool, and "MCP
    implementations are vulnerable to attacks, cascading failures, and loss of human oversight."
  - Only **validated** connectors surface the managed-MCP experience in the portal; **the code-first
    path (REST / SDK / azd) has NO gating — any connector in the catalog can be used.**
  - Requires **Foundry Project Manager** on the project. 14 supported project regions.
  - `azd` extension `microsoft.foundry` bundles `azd ai agent|connection|inspector|project|routine|
    skill|toolbox`.

### Restrict access to sensitive content in Foundry traces (preview)
/azure/foundry/observability/how-to/traces-sensitive-content — ms.date 2026-07-21
  - Seven OpenTelemetry gen-AI attributes are classed as sensitive content:
    `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system_instructions`,
    **`gen_ai.tool.definitions`**, **`gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`**, **`gen_ai.tool.call.result`**,
    `gen_ai.evaluation.explanation`.
  - They are routed to a dedicated Log Analytics table **`AppGenAIContent`**, which can be set
    **Protected** (deny-by-default). Only the **Privileged Monitoring Data Reader** role can then
    read it. Feature flags `protectGenAISensitiveData` / `optOutProtectGenAISensitiveData` on
    `Microsoft.Insights`.
  - **Migration: from September 30, 2026** these attribute values stop being written to
    `AppDependencies` / `AppTraces` / `AppEvents` for newly ingested data — keys remain but values
    are replaced with a pointer to `AppGenAIContent`. Opt-out is discontinued Sept 30, 2027.

### Microsoft Foundry Canvas (preview)
/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/foundry-canvas — ms.date 2026-07-21, updated 2026-07-24
  A **GitHub Copilot App extension** (installed from Settings > Plugins, search `microsoft-foundry`)
  that opens a side panel to design, configure, test and deploy Foundry **hosted agents** from the
  editor. Signs in to Azure, enumerates subscriptions and Foundry projects, and browses the project's
  deployed models, **Toolboxes and tools, skills, and guardrails**. Each canvas choice becomes a
  ready-to-run prompt for Copilot, which writes the agent code in the workspace. "Inspect Locally"
  runs the agent in an embedded **Agent Inspector**; "Deploy to Foundry" publishes it. Both run
  underlying `azd` commands.

### Microsoft Foundry Notification Center
/azure/foundry/concepts/concept-notification-center — ms.date 2026-07-09, updated 2026-07-21
  In-app (Foundry portal) aggregated alert feed for agents, models and projects. Four categories:
  **security alerts from Microsoft Defender for Cloud** (malicious activity, content-safety
  violations, via Azure security alert APIs), **policy and compliance** (Azure Policy + Foundry
  built-in guardrails, ML governance policy violations), and run completion / failure events
  (evaluation runs, training jobs). Bell icon + "View all" page with sort/filter by type, project,
  severity. Delivery is portal-only today.
